items.question: What is Inheritance in Java?
items.answer: Answer: Inheritance is a mechanism in Java in which a child class acquires properties and behavior from a parent class. It promotes code reuse and is implemented using the extends keyword.

items.question: What are the different types of Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: The six types of inheritance covered are: Single Inheritance Multilevel Inheritance Hierarchical Inheritance Hybrid Inheritance Multiple Inheritance Cyclic Inheritance

items.question: Which types of Inheritance are supported by Java through classes?
items.answer: Answer: Java supports: Single Inheritance Multilevel Inheritance Hierarchical Inheritance Hybrid Inheritance Multiple Inheritance and Cyclic Inheritance are not supported through classes.

items.question: What is the standard naming convention for a Java package?

items.question: How can a Java class be renamed in an IDE?
items.answer: Answer: A class can be renamed by selecting the class and using the Refactor → Rename option.

items.question: What is Single Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Single Inheritance is a type of inheritance in which one child class inherits from one parent class. Parent ↓ Child

items.question: How is Single Inheritance implemented in Java?
What members can a child class access through inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: A child class can access inherited members according to their access level. Non-private members can be inherited and accessed according to Java access-control rules, while private members are not directly accessible in the child class.

items.question: What output is produced when the inherited and child members are printed in Single Inheritance?
What is Multilevel Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Multilevel Inheritance is a type of inheritance in which one class inherits from another class and a third class inherits from the second class. Demo3 ↓ Demo4 ↓ Demo5

items.question: How is Multilevel Inheritance implemented in Java?
Which members can the derived class access in multilevel inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: For the hierarchy: Demo3 → Demo4 → Demo5 Demo5 can access: a, b, c, d, e, f The members are available through the inheritance chain.

items.question: What is Hierarchical Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Hierarchical Inheritance is a type of inheritance in which multiple child classes inherit from the same parent class. Sample / \ Sample1 Sample2

items.question: How is Hierarchical Inheritance implemented in Java?
What members can the child classes access in Hierarchical Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Sample1 can access: a, b, c Sample2 can access: a, b, d

items.question: What is the output of the hierarchical inheritance example?
items.answer: Answer: The values are: 100 200 300 100 200 400

items.question: What is Hybrid Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Hybrid Inheritance is a combination of two or more types of inheritance. A combination of hierarchical and multilevel inheritance can form a hybrid structure. Sample / \ Sample1 Sample2 | | Sample3 Sample4

items.question: How is Hybrid Inheritance implemented in Java?
What members can Sample3 and Sample4 access in Hybrid Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Sample3 can access: a, b, c, e Sample4 can access: a, b, d, f

items.question: What is Multiple Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Multiple Inheritance is a type of inheritance in which one child class attempts to inherit from more than one parent class. Parent1 Parent2 \ / Child

items.question: Does Java support Multiple Inheritance through classes?
Why does Java not support Multiple Inheritance through classes?
What is the Diamond Problem?
items.answer: Answer: The Diamond Problem refers to ambiguity that can arise when a child class receives the same member through multiple inheritance paths. Parent / \ Parent1 Parent2 \ / Child

items.question: How can Multiple Inheritance create ambiguity?
What happens when a Java class attempts to extend two classes?
What is Cyclic Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Cyclic Inheritance occurs when classes form a circular inheritance relationship. System1 → System2 → System3 → System1

items.question: How does Cyclic Inheritance occur in Java?
What errors can indicate Cyclic Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Errors associated with a cyclic hierarchy include: hierarchy is inconsistent cycle detected a cycle exists in the type hierarchy

items.question: Why is Cyclic Inheritance not permitted in Java?
items.answer: Answer: Cyclic Inheritance is not permitted because it can lead to infinite constructor chaining. For example: Demo2 constructor ↓ Demo1 constructor ↓ Demo2 constructor ↓ Demo1 constructor ↓ ...

items.question: What are the main problems associated with Multiple and Cyclic Inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Multiple Inheritance can lead to ambiguity through the Diamond Problem. Cyclic Inheritance can lead to infinite constructor chaining.

items.question: What is a constructor in Java?
items.answer: Answer: A constructor is a special member of a class used for initializing an object. It is executed when an object is created.

items.question: Which members do not participate in inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: Two important categories are: Constructors Private members Constructors are not inherited, and private members are not directly accessible in the child class.

items.question: What is constructor chaining in inheritance?
What is the purpose of super() in constructor chaining?
items.answer: Answer: super() is used to invoke the constructor of the parent class. It ensures that the parent constructor executes before the child constructor.

items.question: What is the execution order of constructors in an inheritance hierarchy?
items.answer: Answer: Constructors execute from the topmost superclass toward the child class. For example: Object ↓ Demo1 ↓ Demo2 The order is: Object constructor Demo1 constructor Demo2 constructor

items.question: What happens when an object of a child class is created?
items.answer: Answer: When a child object is created: Memory is allocated for the object. The child constructor is invoked. Constructor chaining moves control to the parent constructor. Parent constructors execute. Control returns toward the child constructor. The child constructor executes.

items.question: What output is produced when both parent and child constructors print messages?
What is the relationship between the Object class and other Java classes?
items.answer: Answer: Object is the top-level superclass in the Java class hierarchy. A class that does not explicitly extend another class implicitly has Object as its superclass.

items.question: When is extends Object implicitly provided?
What happens when a class already extends another class?
How are inherited variables initialized during constructor chaining?
Are constructors inherited by subclasses?
items.answer: Answer: No. Constructors are not inherited by subclasses. However, a parent constructor executes when a child object is created because of constructor chaining.

items.question: Are private members directly accessible in subclasses?
What happens to parent private members when a child object is created?
items.answer: Answer: The child class cannot directly access the private members of the parent. The parent class constructor can still execute its own initialization as part of the constructor chain. The important distinction is that private members are not directly available to the child through inheritance.

items.question: What is variable shadowing in a parameterized constructor?
How is variable shadowing resolved using the this keyword?
When does the compiler provide a default no-argument constructor?
items.answer: Answer: The compiler provides a default no-argument constructor only when no constructor is declared in the class. If a class already contains a constructor, the compiler does not automatically add another no-argument constructor.

items.question: What happens when a class contains only a parameterized constructor?
What happens when a child constructor implicitly calls super() but the parent class has only a parameterized constructor?
items.answer: Answer: The child constructor attempts to invoke a no-argument parent constructor through super(). If the parent class has only a parameterized constructor, there is no matching no-argument constructor, so compilation fails.

items.question: Why does the compiler not automatically provide arguments to a parameterized parent constructor?
items.answer: Answer: The compiler follows predefined rules and does not assume which values should be passed to a parameterized constructor. Therefore, the required arguments must be supplied explicitly.

items.question: How can a child constructor explicitly invoke a parameterized parent constructor?
What happens when the parent class has only a parameterized constructor and the child does not explicitly call it?
What is the correct order for analyzing constructor execution in inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: The constructor flow should be followed from the child toward the parent and then back toward the child: Child constructor ↓ super(...) ↓ Parent constructor ↓ super(...) ↓ Object constructor ↓ Return toward child The parent constructors complete before the child constructor continues.

items.question: What is the key rule of constructor execution in inheritance?
items.answer: Answer: The superclass constructor must execute before the subclass constructor. Constructor chaining through super() establishes this execution order and allows parent-class initialization to occur before child-class initialization.
